Thus $H_1'=H_1$. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction},
with attachments $A$ and the fixed planar graph on $A$
with edge set $E$, lists every possible $H_1$. Adjoining $H_0$ to each gives every
possible $G$, but the enumeration~\supp{E1} excludes
all resulting graphs. Hence no bridge contains such a path.

vertex names: Psi_1 as in Section 4: twins p, q on {s1, s2, s3} and r, z on {t1, t2, t3}. Interior vertices of B are i0, i1, ...
the case: A = {s1, t1, s2, t2} and E = {s1s2, t1t2}. G = H0 ∪ B, where H0 consists of p, q, r, z, their twelve edges and s3t3, and B (called H1 in the proof) meets H0 in A. The candidates are the graphs B of Construction 3.17 with attachments A and added edges E: A independent in B, interior nonempty and connected, every attachment with an interior neighbour, and B + E nonplanar (each candidate gives a Kuratowski subgraph).

verdicts.K5 minor: branch sets in G, or in B + E, which is a minor of G (paths s1 p s2 and t1 r t2)
verdicts.proper nontoroidal minor: either an allowed reduction B' of B with B' + E nonplanar, which makes H0 ∪ B' nontoroidal by the implication proved in Lemma 4.10, or an edge of G = H0 ∪ B whose deletion or contraction leaves a minor model of some T_i
verdicts.excluded by a hypothesis of the case: B has no disjoint s1-t1 and s2-t2 paths; by minimality B is H1, which contains P1 and P2
